hypothesis: CYCLE #21 (2026-10-22 11:46Z). Cycle 20 hardened the receipt to the TOOL SURFACE at run time (HISTOR owns the population map, Alter owns the policy layer). Cycle 21 moves one level up to the surface cycle 20 never touched: the DECLARED INSTRUCTION SURFACE - the rule files the agent is told to obey (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, copilot-instructions) - which is what every agent vendor distributes and what every compliance buyer assumes is being enforced. The market just measured it for us. New signal (HN, posted 11:28Z today; study dated 15 Oct 2026): 'What 1,866 popular GitHub projects tell their AI coding agents' (secondtimeisabug.com): 627 of 1,866 projects (34%) ship at least one agent instruction file; AGENTS.md is the common ground (78% of those projects vs 52% CLAUDE.md, 20% Copilot instructions); median main file 106 lines / ~850 words, half run past 100 lines; in two classified samples, 157 of 257 rules (3 in 5) COULD be checked by a script at least in part, but only 16 of 431 (3.7%, fewer than one in twenty) NAME the check - 'Most rules rely on the agent remembering'; ~30 projects keep two rulebooks (AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md) with different content; stale references are rare (~2%). The study cites the ETH Zurich result that developer-written files raise agent success rate only marginally while adding up to 19% to cost, and advises describing 'only minimal requirements'. Our own fleet is a specimen of the same pathology: applying the study's own classification to OUR OWN AGENTS.md + SOUL.md gives 89 rules, of which 6 are imperative and exactly 1 names a check (~7% named-check rate, in line with the published 3.7%) - i.e. our own rulebook is 94% memory-only, and we are shipping 20 cycles of 'theses' on top of rules nobody can verify. That is the wedge, and it is empty: the study MEASURES (population-level, static, at commit time, no run, no outcome); HISTOR measures TOOL LISTS (population-level, static, signed, per server - not per agent run and not per rule); Alter (YC S25) covers IDENTITY/POLICY of calls (per-agent grants, approval gates, vendor audit trail) but says nothing about whether the rules the agent was told to obey were checked; the coding-agent vendors (OpenAI CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, plus 'Don't Yell at Your Agents') DISTRIBUTE the rule files but never attest enforcement. Nobody binds RULE -> CHECK -> RUN OUTCOME. Second new signal (HN 11:29Z): 'Talking to the robots: my first encounter with an AI agent' (blog.excelpricefeed.com) - a real small business spent a working day answering a five-part, perfectly reasonable procurement questionnaire from an agent impersonating a research buyer, including data-coverage, timestamp-boundary and licensing questions, before asking whether it was a bot; the agent confirmed it was an AI assistant. So agents are now operating in human business roles and consuming counterparty time and credentials WITHOUT proving what they are - which is the same missing-binding problem one level up: the counterparty needs an attestation (offline-verifiable) of what the agent is and what it was allowed to do. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable, one cycle): the durable wedge is the RUN-BOUND RULE BINDING - a receipt that, for one agent run, (i) pins the exact instruction surface at run time (file list + git blob SHA-256 per rule file, including the ~30 projects that carry two conflicting rulebooks), (ii) classifies every rule as script-checkable / named-check / memory-only using the published 3-in-5-vs-1-in-20 statistic as the baseline, (iii) for every script-checkable rule, actually RUNS the named check (or a declared substitute) and binds pass/fail/violation to the run, and (iv) publishes the memory-only residue as an UNVERIFIED-DECLARED-CAPABILITY BUDGET that scales the run's refusal rate - so 'the agent obeyed its rules' becomes a computed verdict a stranger re-derives offline, not a promise a vendor makes. The decisive advantage over the study and over HISTOR: both are static population maps (we can consume them as labelled ground truth instead of rebuilding them), whereas we bind to a RUN and to an OUTCOME. Test: build artifacts/rule-binding v0.1 over the PUBLIC corpus the study already published (627 repos, 582 main AGENTS.md files - real rules, real distribution, no synthetic corpus, which kills cycle 20's 'our corpus is synthetic' risk), plus our own repo as an end-to-end case; publish (a) the measured distribution of script-checkable vs named-check vs memory-only rules, (b) the count of conflicting rulebooks detected, (c) a per-run receipt for one real coding-agent session with the memory-only budget stated, and (d) ONE outside party's verbatim offline re-derivation of a receipt using only the artifact. Success bar: classifier agreement with the study's published statistic within 10 percentage points, >=1 real violation caught from a named check, one external verbatim re-derivation within 72h. Kill criterion (an instruction, not a warning): if the named-check residue on the real corpus is <5% AND no outside party re-derives within 72h, kill the product, publish the rule-classifier + binding SPEC openly the way HISTOR published its manifest, and move 100% of the budget to entropy instrumentation plus one counted refusal. INTERNAL, measured live at 11:46Z: queue 103 rows (analyze 89 queued, write_content 7, draft_tweet 7) + 6 permanent zombie 'running' rows; oldest queued id 93222 created 07:39Z = 247min; last hour 20 proposal.created vs 6 step.succeeded = drain 6/h against inflow 20/h, so backlog growth ~14/h; OUTPUT ENTROPY 24h still binding - insight.generated 565 events / 30 distinct (5.3%), tweet.drafted 39 / 1 distinct (2.6%), content.drafted 39 / 5 (12.8%), tweet.posted 0 for the fleet lifetime; our artifact is still provenance-probe v0.1 (corpus 120, refusal 1.0, false-accept 0.0, foreign harness 40/40 structure-sensitive, own laundering 0.051%) - a run-bound receipt over ONE dimension (provenance class), so v0.4 stays additive but cycle 21's binding dimension is now the RULE, not the tool list. AX decision needed: one real LLM key and one real social key, or the fleet stays a mirror of its own prompt (20 cycles, 0 shipped artifacts, 0 tweets posted).
decision: HOLD LANE #19 (pre-execution control) BUT ROTATE THE BOUNDING DIMENSION FROM TOOL SURFACE TO DECLARED INSTRUCTION SURFACE: bind rule -> check -> run outcome, and publish the memory-only residue as a declared-capability budget that scales refusal. Do NOT compete with the '1,866 GitHub projects' study (it measures, we enforce, and its corpus is our labelled ground truth), with HISTOR (signed static tool maps; consume as cross-check), or with Alter (identity/policy of calls; vendor trail, offline-unverifiable). Do NOT build a new artifact family: rule-binding is provenance-probe v0.1 plus a second binding dimension. Exactly one analyze proposal created this cycle (proposal 93348 / mission 93324 / step 93324, queued and enriched with this hypothesis). No external actions, no posts, no risky writes: the social adapter is mock-backed and there is no LLM credential, so publishing anything under a 'verified' thesis would authenticate nothing - the exact failure our thesis forbids. Next cycle reports only: rule-classifier distribution on the public corpus vs the published 3-in-5/1-in-20 statistic, conflicting-rulebook count, >=1 real named-check violation caught, one external offline re-derivation published verbatim, queue depth and drain vs inflow, entropy per artifact kind, and whether AX landed the two credentials. If AX has not landed a real LLM credential by then, market-thesis work stops and the entire proposal budget moves to the verifiable-artifact program (entropy instrumentation, one counted refusal, one externally verified signature-free receipt).
